title: Why God Waited for Moses
paragraphs:
Why God Waited for Moses
The Man Who Thought He Missed His Calling—Until God Turned His Greatest Failure Into His Greatest Assignment
There are moments in life that feel impossible to explain.
Moments when you look back and wonder why God allowed so much waiting.
Why everyone else seemed to move forward while you remained stuck in a season that felt forgotten.
Maybe you've asked the question quietly.
Maybe you've cried it into a pillow.
Maybe you've never said it aloud because deep down you're afraid of the answer.
"God, if You were going to use me... why didn't You do it sooner?"
Few people understand that question more than Moses.
Most people remember Moses as the man who split the Red Sea.
But before Moses became the hero of Exodus, he was a scandal.
Before he stood before Pharaoh, he was a fugitive.
Before he carried God's commandments, he carried guilt.
Before he led a nation, he was hiding in a wilderness.
And perhaps that is exactly why God waited.
Israel groaned beneath slavery. Generations had suffered under oppression. The cries of God's people rose before heaven.
Moses was born into that suffering.
Yet from the beginning, his life was surrounded by divine intervention.
Given influence, power, privilege, and access.
If God needed a deliverer, Moses appeared perfectly positioned.
Acts 7:25 says Moses believed his people would understand that God was using him to rescue them.
The problem was not that Moses lacked passion.
The problem was that Moses tried to accomplish God's purpose without God's timing.
One day he saw an Egyptian beating a Hebrew.
He struck the Egyptian and killed him.
Then buried the body in the sand.
The next day Moses discovered that sin never stays buried forever.
The man who thought he would save Israel became a wanted criminal.
Everything he thought God was doing suddenly appeared destroyed.
Many believers live in that same place today.
But all they can see now is the failure.
And because of what happened, they assume God is finished with them.
Moses likely believed the same thing.
By the time God appeared at the burning bush, Moses was eighty years old.
Many people believe eighty is where the story ends.
For Moses, eighty was where the story finally began.
This is where Scripture reveals something profound.
"And the angel of the LORD appeared unto him in a flame of fire out of the midst of a bush."

"וַיֵּרָא מַלְאַךְ יְהוָה אֵלָיו"
Vayyera Mal'akh Adonai Elav
"And the Messenger of Yahweh appeared to him."
Many scholars recognize this as a theophany—a visible manifestation of God Himself.
What Moses discovered in the wilderness was not merely fire.
The place of apparent abandonment became the place of divine revelation.
The years Moses considered wasted were not wasted at all.
God was doing something deeper than preparation for leadership.
Egypt taught Moses how to be somebody.
The wilderness taught Moses he was nobody.
Because a man filled with confidence in himself cannot fully depend on God.
Forty years earlier Moses rushed ahead.
When God called him, Moses immediately argued.
The same man who once acted without permission now feared acting at all.
The wilderness had accomplished what the palace never could.
God wasn't simply waiting to use Moses.
God was preparing Moses to be usable.
Yet throughout Scripture, waiting is rarely punishment.
Even Jesus spent approximately thirty years in relative obscurity before beginning His public ministry.
Heaven is never in a hurry because God is not merely interested in what you accomplish.
He is interested in who you become.
The Greek New Testament often uses the word kairos (καιρός), meaning God's appointed moment, a divinely ordered season distinct from ordinary chronological time.
Human beings think primarily in chronos (χρόνος)—minutes, days, years.
And perhaps that truth reaches into your own story today.
Maybe you feel like everyone else is moving while your life remains frozen.
Maybe your greatest pain isn't what happened.
Maybe your greatest pain is wondering why God hasn't done something yet.
But what if the waiting isn't evidence of God's absence?
What if it is evidence of His craftsmanship?
A master sculptor removes stone before revealing beauty.
A refiner uses fire before revealing purity.
A shepherd leads through valleys before reaching green pastures.
God often works the same way.
The burning bush reveals another breathtaking truth.
When Moses asked God's name, the Lord replied:
"I WILL BE WHAT I WILL BE."
The phrase carries the idea of God's eternal self-existence, faithfulness, and unchanging presence.
God was telling Moses something powerful.
"You do not need to know everything about your future because I already stand inside it."
The answer to Moses' insecurity was not greater confidence in Moses.
The answer was confidence in God.
The solution to your weakness is not discovering how strong you are.
The solution is discovering how faithful Christ is.
And this is where the story points directly to Jesus.
Moses led Israel from physical slavery.
Jesus leads sinners from the slavery of sin.
Jesus established a better covenant through His blood.
Jesus entered death itself and emerged victorious.
Moses' story was marked by scandal before service.
Jesus carried the scandal of our sin upon Himself to secure our salvation.
The Gospel is not the story of qualified people being chosen.
The Gospel is the story of broken people being redeemed.
Yet God rewrote every one of their stories.
"Where sin increased, grace abounded all the more."
That is the heart of the Gospel.
And perhaps that is why God waited for Moses.
Because when Moses finally stood before Pharaoh, nobody could confuse God's power with Moses' ability.
The years of waiting removed every illusion.
The deliverance would belong entirely to God.
The same may be true in your life.
The chapter you call delay may become the chapter that reveals God's glory most clearly.
The wound may become the testimony.
The failure may become the platform.
The wilderness may become the classroom.
The scandal may become the doorway to grace.
Because Jesus specializes in rewriting stories people think are finished.
Maybe that is why you are reading this right now.
But as a reminder that God has not abandoned the work He began in you.
Your testimony may become the encouragement someone else desperately needs today.
You never know who might discover hope through a story God uses to reach them.
Your support helps expand the reach of these messages while bringing glory to God through faithful Gospel-centered content.
Because one day you may discover that the years you thought God wasted were actually the years He used to prepare you for everything He promised.
From Scandal to Grace, the wilderness was never your ending—it was God's editing room.
